methods: Synthesize a decoder with exact coefficients and fully priced helper endpoints.
Bound the best possible budget for a fixed support alphabet before synthesis.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one finite support alphabet and test exact decoding constraints before building a whole network.

allowed_variations: Select a specific masked or overcomplete family with exact labels and supports.
scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Proof obligation inside the masked (E-graph) model: is every rank-<=8 solution of PR1212's system (E) on P112 minus an odd pair (the part of P110 that PR1419's extension lemma cannot reach) equal to D(2G)D^-1, so that decoders with exactly eight costly terms keep PR968's floor 62?
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a masked decoder can beat the floor. PR1212/PR1389/PR1399 answered it for exactly eight costly terms on P120, P112, P111 and every P104 frame complement, and PR1419 for punctures inside a frame; PR1419's open next question is the two odd-pair P110 orbits. This closes them, completing P110; it does not construct a decoder.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the binding complex supplier: masked eight-costly-term decoders cannot beat PR968's floor on any P110 unit, so the remaining masked escape routes are nine or more costly terms or deeper punctures with odd pairs.
stop_rule: Stop at P110; P109 and deeper punctures with an odd pair, and nine or more costly terms, are left as handoffs.
evidence: verify.py: 26 exact checks in about 2 s (orbits of odd pairs; per orbit representative the unit, D4 structure, class profile, (I3), (I4) and gluing, Lemma 9 connectivity and algebra, assembly, CNF consistency, DRUP replay of zero exclusion with its own RUP checker, and two proof controls). PR1212's rup_check independently accepts both proofs (recorded, not run by verify.py).

open_questions.question: Does rank-8 rigidity of (E) hold on P109 units P112 minus X, |X| = 3, where X is not inside a frame of P112 (198688 of 227920 triples)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: With this package and PR1419 every P110 unit is rigid; P109 is the next depth of the eight-term gap in the masked model.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate the FRAME0-stabiliser orbits of the uncovered triples and run make_proof.py's pivot rule and CNF on one representative per orbit (about 1 s per unit at P110); use PR1419's Lemma 10 whenever a rigid sub-unit exists.
open_questions.blocked_by: The orbit count is not yet known, and each orbit needs its own zero-exclusion certificate unless a rigid sub-unit is found.
